issue.title: test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet fails under the full parallel lane: a Textual worker is still unfinished after AcePage exits
issue.description:
REPRODUCTION: tests/test_ace_testing.py::test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet failed once under the full parallel lane during a monitored 'just check-full' at HEAD 423669549 (monitor j529c27q5gye, 2026-08-17): '1 failed, 32563 passed, 13 skipped, 70 warnings in 1144.43s'. It was the ONLY failing node in the run, and its failure is what turned 'just test-cost' (Justfile:401) and therefore check-full red.

EXACT FAILURE (tests/test_ace_testing.py:169, the post-exit block after the 'async with AcePage() as page' body):
    assert all(worker.is_finished for worker in app.workers)
    E       assert False
    E        +  where False = all(<generator object ...<genexpr>>)
Every earlier assertion in that test passed, including the in-context structural-quiet assertions and the three post-exit assertions above it (_fs_watcher/_prompt_source_watcher/_stall_watchdog are None, _pump_free_async_tasks empty). So the app tore down its watchers and timers correctly and only a Textual worker was still unfinished when the context manager returned.

NOT REPRODUCED under narrower lanes (this is the useful negative evidence for whoever picks this up):
  - alone: 1 passed
  - whole module, default lane, 5 consecutive runs: 35 passed each time
  - whole module co-run with the bead/chop tests that landed alongside it: 94 passed
  - 'just test-contention -- tests/test_ace_testing.py' (the instrument sase-ct's retirement policy names): 'contention tally: 0 node(s) failed across 3 repeat(s) in 225.7s; red repeats: none'
That last one matters: pinned-CPU starvation restricted to this file does NOT reproduce it, so the trigger is very likely cross-FILE interaction in the whole-suite lane rather than intra-file load. A fix attempt that only soaks this file will look green while proving nothing.

NOT A PROCESS-GLOBAL-STATE LEAK, at least not one the current detector sees: the same failing run's sase global leak detector reported '0 poisoning change(s) across 0 test(s); 30980 warming mutation(s) filtered; 302 cooling mutation(s) filtered; 1122 invalidation(s) filtered'. So this is a worker/task lifecycle race, distinct in mechanism from the config/registry state-leak nodes that dominate this flake class.

STATUS: this node is NOT in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt and 'grep' over the durable flake-evidence store found no prior failure record for it, so 2026-08-17 is its first recorded sighting.

SCOPE: determine which Textual worker is still running when AcePage.__aexit__ returns under the full lane, then either make the harness await/cancel it deterministically before the assertion or fix the production path that leaves it outstanding. Prefer a mechanism fix over baselining the node; if it has to be baselined first, the baseline entry needs this bead named as owner per the header of tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

PROPOSED BY: the land agent for epic sase-on, which is NOT the cause: that epic's six commits touch zero src/sase/ace/** files and zero ACE tests (they touch bead config/triage/stale-cleanup, notification gate wiring, default_config.yml, sase.schema.json and docs), and the co-run above rules out its new tests interfering.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-ct — the retired umbrella for 'ACE TUI test fails under the full parallel run, passes in isolation'. DO NOT +1 or reopen it; its close reason mandates exactly this route (narrow node-specific bead, RELATED note, re-measure with just test-contention), which is why this bead exists. The contention re-measurement it asks for is in the description and came back clean, so the umbrella's usual intra-file-starvation reproduction does not apply here.
